subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The imposition of lock down proved to be a _________ for many students who were not prepared for the examinations.
solution:
The correct answer is: **'blessing in disguise'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"blessing in disguise"** means something that seems bad or unlucky at first, but results in something good in the end. (वेश बदलकर आई हुई आशीर्वाद)

 
 
• **Example: **Losing that job was a **blessing in disguise** because it pushed me to start my own business.
 
 
 
• In the context of the sentence, the lockdown initially appears to be a hindrance.
 
• For students who were not prepared for their examinations, it turned out to be beneficial.
 
• The lockdown may have given them extra time to study.
 
• This makes "**blessing in disguise**" the most appropriate choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

**Complete Sentence:** *The imposition of lock down proved to be a blessing in disguise__ for many students who were not prepared for the examinations.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Feather in cap** (गर्व की बात): An achievement or honour that someone can be proud of.

 
 
• **Example:** Winning the award was a real **feather in her cap**.
 
 
 
• **Piece of cake** (बिल्कुल आसान काम): Something that is very easy to do.
 
 
• **Example:** The test was a **piece of cake**; I finished it in 10 minutes.
 
 
 
• **Chip on their shoulder** (किसी बात का गुस्सा होना): A person has a habit of holding a grudge or feeling resentful.
 
 
• **Example:** He has a **chip on his shoulder** about not getting promoted.
